evidence: "Floyd-Warshall" in both surviving solutions, followed by their subset-based terminal-connectivity computation; this relies on shortest paths through non-primary vertices.
affordance_in_statement: The remaining facilities on campus are secondary. You are free to install links that pass through these secondary facilities if it helps lower the overall expense, or you may ignore them entirely.
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving way to remove this: it is the defining Steiner-tree feature of the task. If changing the task is permitted, replace the secondary-facility permission with a rule that every installed link must have two primary endpoints.

common_affordance: The explicit permission to use secondary facilities as intermediate Steiner vertices while requiring connectivity only among primary facilities.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It computes shortest-path distances between primary facilities and then treats the result as a terminal MST, which cannot account for sharing secondary vertices and edges in a Steiner tree.
It similarly computes all-pairs shortest paths among primary nodes and uses a terminal-only MST-style solution, missing cheaper shared routes through secondary facilities.

recommended_edit: If a task change is acceptable, replace the secondary-facility permission with: "Every installed fiber link must connect two primary facilities; secondary facilities cannot be endpoints or intermediate points of an installed link." This removes the Steiner-tree affordance and makes the intended problem a terminal MST.
regression_risk: Restricting links to primary endpoints would accidentally make qwen3-coder and glm-5 correct, because their terminal-MST approach matches that altered task.
